clue.text: Gazing outside carvery in the centre, very hungry

indicators.note: the word for gazing goes around the other piece, sitting outside it

parts.note: gazing means staring

indicators.note: only the central letter of the seven-letter word carvery is used

explanation.surface: Someone peering at a carvery counter, ravenous for the roast.
explanation.definitionFit: Starving is the everyday hyperbole for being extremely hungry, a close synonym.

clue.text: Problem over a style of wresting

parts.note: a sum is an arithmetic problem
O is the cricket scoring abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: A query about a particular wrestling technique.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed clue says 'wresting', a slip for 'wrestling'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sumo is the Japanese form of heavyweight wrestling, so it is one example of a style.

clue.text: Imposing area in Georgian city

parts.note: august means majestic or imposing

explanation.surface: An impressive district in a city in the American state of Georgia.
explanation.definitionFit: Augusta is a city in the US state of Georgia, home of the Masters golf course.

clue.text: A VIP accent I made out in team member

indicators.note: letters made out are worked into something new, so these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dignitary's accent is detected in one of the players.
explanation.definitionFit: A vice-captain is the deputy leader of a sports side, one particular player in it.

clue.text: Stockings, new, only ruined by son

indicators.note: ruined suggests the word only is wrecked and its letters scrambled

parts.note: S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A boy has laddered the only new pair of hosiery.
explanation.definitionFit: Nylons are women's stockings, named after the synthetic fibre they are made from.

clue.text: Couple I came upon heading west

indicators.note: in an across clue heading west means reading right to left, so the word is backwards

parts.note: came upon means met, encountered

explanation.surface: A traveller describes running into a pair while going west.
explanation.definitionFit: An item is a romantically linked couple, an informal idiom.

clue.text: Flavour containing hint of walnut, in a manner of speaking

indicators.note: the flavour word holds the other letter within it

parts.note: tang is a sharp flavour

indicators.note: a hint is a small trace, here just the opening letter of walnut

explanation.surface: Tasting a dish with a touch of walnut, so to speak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a manner of speaking' looks like a link phrase, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A twang is a nasal accent or distinctive quality of voice, a way of talking.

clue.text: Reflect upon friend taking rewrite on board

indicators.note: taking something on board means absorbing it, so one word goes inside the other
completes the phrase taking on board, the containment signal

parts.note: mate is an informal word for friend
to edit is to rewrite text

explanation.surface: Pondering a pal who has accepted a revision of their work.
explanation.definitionFit: To meditate upon something is to ponder or contemplate it deeply.

clue.text: Wonderful conjuring

definitions.meaning: informally, something wonderful is described as brilliant or terrific
conjuring is the performance of tricks and illusions

explanation.surface: Praise for a marvellous stage trick.
explanation.definitionFit: Magic serves both as slang for marvellous and as the name for conjuring tricks.

clue.text: Line with an enclosure, cord round one's neck

parts.note: a yard is an enclosed area of ground

explanation.surface: Describes a rope fixed to a fence, which turns out to be worn around the neck.
explanation.definitionFit: A lanyard is a cord worn about the neck to hold a badge, whistle or key.

clue.text: Funny name sounds about right for a popular aria

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go around the other letter
funny suggests the words are oddly arranged, so their letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: A comic remark that an odd title sounds correct for a well-known song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Funny' makes the anagram NESSUNDOMA, and 'about' wraps it around R. 'sounds' looks like a homophone signal but is plain fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Nessun Dorma is the tenor showpiece from Puccini's Turandot, made famous to football fans by Pavarotti.

clue.text: Clairvoyance of backer, before quote read out

parts.note: to second a motion is to back it, so a seconder or second is a backer

indicators.note: spoken aloud, the word for quote is heard as a word for vision

parts.note: to cite is to quote

explanation.surface: A supporter's psychic powers, shown before a quotation is spoken.
explanation.definitionFit: Second sight is the supposed power to see future or distant events, a synonym.

clue.text: One's label confused a girl

parts.note: one is I, so one's is I plus S

indicators.note: confused means mixed up, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Someone muddles a tag meant for a young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Isabella is a female first name, given as an example of a girl.

clue.text: Irritable secret agent snatching quick kip

indicators.note: snatching means grabbing hold of, so one word clutches the other inside it

parts.note: a spy is a secret agent
a nap is a short sleep

explanation.surface: A grumpy undercover operative grabbing forty winks.
explanation.definitionFit: Snappy means short-tempered and liable to speak sharply, a synonym.

clue.text: Issued suitable clothes

parts.note: out can mean published or issued
fit means suitable or appropriate

explanation.surface: Appropriate garments have been handed out.
explanation.definitionFit: An outfit is a set of clothes worn together.

clue.text: Goods about to be put in box

indicators.note: signals the second piece being placed inside the first

parts.note: to box is to fight
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Merchandise is about to be packed into a crate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'box' reads as a container but is the verb to fight.
explanation.definitionFit: Freight is goods carried as cargo by lorry, rail, ship or aircraft.

clue.text: One consulted for advice: nothing clear, surprisingly

parts.note: O is the zero shape standing for nothing

indicators.note: surprisingly hints the letters turn up in an unexpected order

explanation.surface: An adviser whose guidance, oddly, is far from clear.
explanation.definitionFit: An oracle is a source of wise counsel, originally a priestess consulted for prophecy.

clue.text: A rude beggar silly to harbour resentment

indicators.note: silly suggests the words are made nonsensical, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An impolite tramp is foolish to hold a grievance.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to keep feeling bitterness towards someone over a past wrong.

clue.text: Racecourse in Nova Scotia

indicators.note: in signals letters found inside the words Nova Scotia

explanation.surface: Points to a horse-racing track in the Canadian province.
explanation.definitionFit: Ascot is a famous English racecourse in Berkshire, host of Royal Ascot.

clue.text: Slight scout leader unknotted ropes, initially

indicators.note: initially picks the opening letter of each of the four following words

explanation.surface: A minor embarrassment: the scout leader's ropes came untied.
explanation.definitionFit: A slight and a slur are both insults that disparage someone.

clue.text: Saying few words, endlessly beat a cheat inside

indicators.note: the phrase a cheat goes inside the shortened word
endlessly means the word for beat loses its final letter

parts.note: to lick is to beat or thrash
a con is a swindle or cheat

explanation.surface: A terse remark: thrash a swindler without end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' leaves LIC, and 'inside' places the other pieces within it.
explanation.definitionFit: Laconic means using very few words, terse in speech.

clue.text: Splendid beer knocked back

indicators.note: knocked back suggests drinking, but here the word for beer is turned backwards

parts.note: lager is a type of beer

explanation.surface: Praise for a pint downed in one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked back' looks like drinking slang but is the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Regal means kingly, so magnificent or splendid in style.

clue.text: Singer, off-key a lot

indicators.note: off-key means out of tune, signalling the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A vocalist who is often out of tune.
explanation.definitionFit: An alto is a singer with a low female or high male voice range.

clue.text: Put off drinking tin, gets bottle

indicators.note: drinking means taking in, so one word swallows the other

parts.note: to deter is to put off or discourage
a can is a tin

explanation.surface: Someone discouraged from drinking from a tin reaches for a bottle instead.
explanation.definitionFit: A decanter is a stoppered glass bottle for serving wine or spirits.
